title: Optional and java.time
description:
A staff directory keeps people by id. Write it with `Optional` for everything that may be missing, and dates with `java.time`:

```java
// Person.java
record Person(String id, String name, String managerId, String city, LocalDate born) { }   // managerId and city may be null

// Directory.java
class Directory {
    Directory(List<Person> people)
    Optional<Person> find(String id)
    Optional<String> managerName(String id)            // the name of the person's manager, if both exist
    String cityOf(String id)                           // the city, or "unknown" when the person or the city is missing
    Optional<Person> oldest()
    static int age(LocalDate born, LocalDate today)    // whole years
    static long daysUntilBirthday(LocalDate born, LocalDate today)   // 0 on the birthday; Feb 29 birthdays count on Feb 28 in other years
}
```

Use `map`, `flatMap`, `filter` and `orElse` rather than `isPresent()` and `get()`.

starter.Person.java:
import java.time.LocalDate;

record Person(String id, String name, String managerId, String city, LocalDate born) { }

solution.Person.java:
import java.time.LocalDate;

record Person(String id, String name, String managerId, String city, LocalDate born) { }

hints: `find(id).map(Person::managerId)` is empty when the person or their manager id is missing (`map` turns a `null` result into empty); `flatMap(this::find)` then looks up the manager, which may be missing too.

`Period.between(born, today).getYears()` gives whole years; `date.withYear(y)` moves a date to another year (and turns February 29 into February 28 when needed). `a.isBefore(b)` tells whether date `a` comes before date `b`, and `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between(a, b)` counts the days from `a` to `b`.
rules: Chain map, flatMap, filter and orElse instead of isPresent and get.

rules.message: Chain map, flatMap, filter and orElse instead of isPresent and get.
